correctness.rationale: Exact two-by-two algebra reduces inverse Euclidean norm to positivity of J-transpose-J minus I, whose trace is positive. Its determinant is an explicit convex quadratic in cosine twice the angle; whenever the unrestricted minimum is negative or zero the minimizing cosine is shown to lie strictly inside the physically allowed interval. The derived frontier and unique threshold follow by one-variable calculus. An independent fixed rational counterexample separates strict monotonicity and inverse nonexpansivity. A standalone exact-rational checker passed 1734 tests, but unrestricted correctness relies on the written proof.

value.rationale: Inverse constitutive evaluation and its local sensitivity are natural requirements for nonlinear magnetic numerical solvers. The exact all-angle condition quantifies the minimum sliding-response factor preventing Euclidean error amplification as a function of two measurable susceptibility parameters. A rational example establishes a concrete failure of using strict forward monotonicity as a surrogate conditioning test. This precise quantitative boundary is pertinent even without a larger solver convergence theorem.
